youngest_loss.date_caveat: git commit date; true submit may be EARLIER, which makes the loss OLDER not younger — so read as loss at >=37d

method: 25 prefix probes spanning every job-id prefix cited by findings, plus a 173-job banking sweep
cause_separation: RETENTION, not account access. The account hypothesis cannot produce a split between two jobs on the SAME BACKEND one day apart with the same job-id prefix; a clock does exactly that. Every prefix older than d9b is lost, every prefix from d9b (2026-07-14) onward is retrievable.
consequence: Anything flown before ~2026-07-13 has PERMANENTLY lost its calibration window. This is a hard deadline on every sigma-headline finding not yet epoch-labelled, and it is why windows had to be banked before labels: a label is reversible work available forever, a window is not.
